<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys"></a>

## Radio contact, operating times and an unavailable key

**Sources on this page:** p142 A. [Concise case study](../radio/radio_contacts_and_keys.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p100 C](100.md#source-p100-c), [p137 D](137.md#source-p137-d), [p150 A2](150.md#source-p150-a2).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-radio-contact-operating-times-and-an-unavailable-key"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

These four independent records describe a broken wire connection, timed
radio calls, an embassy receiving station and the local absence of an
`OSKACHI` key. They use unchanged previously published keys and complete
source frames. They are grouped by subject, not asserted to be one exchange.

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [collected intercepts](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [inputs](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/inputs.json) and
[certificates](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/certificates.json)
retain exact source rows, headers, key provenance, image hashes, raw readings
and all local repairs. Printed page numbers are three less than PDF page numbers.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-p100-c-direct-contact-while-the-wire-is-broken"></a>

### p100 C: direct contact while the wire is broken

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p100_C.png)
is under a November 1 heading, with this November 2 reception line:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
C) UKS v ZÖN (2.03 a.m., November 2nd)
2235 (1) AN LP
RIZI-158
```

</details>

All 158 coordinates give 79 fixed plaintext labels under `Nov1-3`, without
any repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WANNISTUNMITTELBARERVERKEHRMITEUCHXMUENCHENODERBRSLAUMEGLICHXDRAHTUNTERBROCHENX
```

</details>

The sender asks when direct communication with the recipient, Munich or
the place written `BRSLAU` will be possible, and says the wire connection
is interrupted. `BRSLAU` is naturally read as Breslau and `MEGLICH` as a
damaged spelling of *möglich*, but **both remain literal in the certificate**.
No missing plaintext letters are inserted. The separately printed
[p100 B](../military/budapest_wire_break.md) gives a longer wire-break report;
this does not by itself prove a single transmission or a specific route.

This is distinct from the [p100 challenge](../p100.md), whose earlier
Belgrade body remains credited to Armin.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-p137-d-the-oskachi-key-is-no-longer-here"></a>

### p137 D: the OSKACHI key is no longer here

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p137_D.png)
has `RIZI-102`. Its upper sender initial is overprinted, so the header is
conservatively retained as:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
D) ?CO V OSM (1.55 November 5th,)
RIZI-102
NF NRO V OSM
```

</details>

The page heading is November 6. Neither it nor the footer is used to resolve
the unclear upper callsign or the time's missing a.m./p.m. designation.
The two dots after the final cipher group `AX` are punctuation; the footer
is outside the 102-coordinate body.

All 51 raw plaintext positions are fixed under `Nov4-6`:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
POTSAGENDA3SSCHLUESSELOSKACHIHIERNICHTMEHRVORHANDEN
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate substitution, source **79: G→X**, changes the `3`
inside `DA3S` to `S`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
POTSAGENDASSSCHLUESSELOSKACHIHIERNICHTMEHRVORHANDEN
```

</details>

Readable German:

**Readable German:**

> POT sagen, dass Schlüssel OSKACHI hier nicht mehr vorhanden.

It asks that POT be told the `OSKACHI` key is no longer available here.
The key name itself is unchanged. The message does **not** say why it is
unavailable, identify a specific square or rank order, give its operating
period, or connect it to a separate challenge ciphertext. Its presence
inside a telegram decoded with `Nov4-6` does not make `OSKACHI` another name
for that transport key.

The raw numeral `3` remains visible in the original reading and numerical
ledger. Its local word repair does not reassign the square's digit `3`.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-p142-a-0430-calling-signal-then-listen-again-at-0645"></a>

### p142 A: 0430 calling signal, then listen again at 0645

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p142_A.png)
is headed November 6:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) NKJ ZÖN v LP (08.25 p.m., November 6th)
FUER ZÖN 1900 (6/11)
RIZI-128
```

</details>

All 128 coordinates and 64 plaintext labels are fixed under `Nov4-6`, with
no substitutions or fills:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GEBENSIEX0430X10XMINXVVVXDANNIHREFKSPRUNDHOERENSIEUNSWIEDERX0645
```

</details>

The instruction is to send **10 minutes of `VVV` at 0430**, then the
recipient's radiograms (`FKSPR`), and listen again at **0645**. All three
numerical fields are literal published-square readings. No extra day or
time zone is inferred from the evening reception time.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-p150-a2-receiving-station-in-the-embassy"></a>

### p150 A2: receiving station in the embassy

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p150_A2.png)
explicitly labels this **part 2**. Its first part has not been attached or
reconstructed in this edition:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) LP v NKJ (8.55 p.m., November 7th)
PERA OSMAINE 6/11
FUER EILKESE ZU SS D (5) 2200
2 TL RICHI-180
UMGEHEND WEITERGEBEN
```

</details>

The page heading is November 6. The literal `OSMAINE` and `EILKESE` spellings
and the November 7 reception remain unchanged. The instruction separator
before `UMGEHEND WEITERGEBEN` is outside the ciphertext.

The 180-slot source contains one dash and gives 89 fixed labels out of 90
under `Nov4-6`:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
JEDOCHHOERTEMPEGSSTMTXINBOTSCHAFTAUFEUCHXNAMEXQZXXADT?SSENCHIFFRITENXINMLLENPERIDENANRUFEN
```

</details>

Six known-coordinate substitutions and one dash fill give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
JEDOCHHOERTEMPFGSSTATXINBOTSCHAFTAUFEUCHXNAMEXQZXXADRESSENCHIFFRIRENXINALLENPERIDENANRUFEN
```

</details>

The receiving station (`EMPFGSSTAT`) in the embassy listens for the
recipient. The message supplies the literal name/separator field
`NAMEXQZXX`, asks for addresses to be enciphered, and says to call in every
period. **The precise name boundary within `QZXX` is left unresolved.**
`CHIFFRIREN` and `PERIDEN` remain literal spellings; no extra plaintext
letters are claimed. The opening `JEDOCH` is retained rather than inventing
the missing preceding clause.

Known-coordinate changes, all at zero-based source indices:
**23 X→V, 80 X→V, 86 F→A, 92 X→V, 150 A→V, 167 X→V**.
The separate printed-dash fill is **112 ?→A**. Two of those substitutions
jointly change one raw `E` to `F` in `EMPFGSSTAT`; the certificate does not
collapse their cost into a single coordinate repair.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-verify-and-prior-credit"></a>

### Verify and prior credit

```sh
python experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/verify.py --verify
```

The independent standard-library verifier rebuilds every source witness,
checks raw domains and numerical fields, and prices substitutions separately
from source-dash fills. No source coordinate is inserted or removed and no
published square is changed. Re-encryption confirms this stated arithmetic,
not the unique history of a damaged word or the identities of station names.

The keys are prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno
Wacker**, [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also published in George Lasry's [2017-02-24 comment 4](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).
Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates existed. The bounded author-paper
check found no explicit examples of these bodies; it does not establish
universal first-decipherment priority.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-representative-retention"></a>

## The Caucasus K.M. representative is to remain

**Sources on this page:** p142 B. [Concise case study](../caucasus/representative_retention.md).

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-representative-retention-the-caucasus-km-representative-is-to-remain"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This p142 B telegram replies to an earlier message and says the `BEV K.M.`
representative in the Caucasus, at Tiflis, is to remain. The closing names
the `KRIEGSAMT KRIEGSROHSTOFFABTLG`. The abbreviated office `K.M.` is left
unexpanded; the closing alone is not used to assign it a different title.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-representative-retention-source-and-reading"></a>

### Source and reading

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p142, PDF p145](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [B crop](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p142_B.png)
is under a November 6 heading:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) NKJ v LP (08.30 p.m., November 6th)
FUER COS EINMAL 1250 (6/11)
RICHI-286
```

</details>

All **286 coordinates** are visible and valid, matching the printed length.
The earlier 280-slot OCR extraction omitted source content and is not the
analysis frame. The unchanged published `Nov4-6` key fixes all 143 raw labels:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FUERXBEVXKMXKAUKASUCXT9FLISXZU4TELEGRAMMVOMX29X10X18XPOTX44XNRX2331XBEVXKXMXSOLLBLEIBENXKRIEGSAMTKRIEGSROHSTOFFABTLGXNRXZXROEMX1XAX23X11X18XKRA
```

</details>

Three observed-coordinate substitutions give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
FUERXBEVXKMXKAUKASUSXTIFLISXZUMTELEGRAMMVOMX29X10X18XPOTX44XNRX2331XBEVXKXMXSOLLBLEIBENXKRIEGSAMTKRIEGSROHSTOFFABTLGXNRXZXROEMX1XAX23X11X18XKRA
```

</details>

Readable core:

**Readable German:**

> Für Bev. K.M. Kaukasus, Tiflis. Zum Telegramm vom 29.10.18,
> POT 44, Nr. 2331. Bev. K.M. soll bleiben.

The source uses `BEVXKMX` in the address and `BEVXKXM` later; both exact
separator patterns remain in the encoded edition. The following reference
is retained verbatim and **not silently interpreted as a November date**:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — unchanged reference-field excerpt:**

```text
KRIEGSAMTKRIEGSROHSTOFFABTLGXNRXZXROEMX1XAX23X11X18XKRA
```

</details>

| Source index, zero-based | Printed group / position, one-based | Change | Effect |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 52 | 11 / 3 | `F` → `V` | `T9FLIS` → `TIFLIS` |
| 53 | 11 / 4 | `V` → `F` | `ZU4TELEGRAMM` → `ZUMTELEGRAMM` |
| 171 | 35 / 2 | `D` → `G` | `KAUKASUC` → `KAUKASUS` |

The raw `9` and `4` within words are separately preserved in the numerical
ledger. Their local repairs do not reassign square digits. All actual date,
number and reference fields remain unchanged. There are no erasure fills,
coordinate insertions, deletions or square changes.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-representative-retention-reproduce-and-prior-credit"></a>

### Reproduce and prior credit

The [source inputs](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/inputs.json)
and [certificate](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/certificates.json)
retain raw domains, changes and the complete forward witness.

```sh
python experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/verify.py --verify
```

The published key is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461).
Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates existed. No universal first-reading
priority is asserted. The exact repaired witness establishes its stated
three-coordinate cost, not the identity of the representative or proof that
the instruction was carried out.

<a id="edition-cases-military-dobrudscha-report"></a>

## Request for a position on a Dobrudscha report

**Sources on this page:** p142 C. [Concise case study](../military/dobrudscha_report.md).

<a id="edition-cases-military-dobrudscha-report-request-for-a-position-on-a-dobrudscha-report"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p142 C asks for a response to an Entente report of renewed Romanian
occupation of the Dobrudscha. The message is addressed to the literal
`N.O. MACKENSEN` field and closes with `ABT FREMDE HEERE`. This edition
recovers the report's wording; it does not independently establish the
military event or expand the abbreviated addressee's office.

<a id="edition-cases-military-dobrudscha-report-source-and-reading"></a>

### Source and reading

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p142, PDF p145](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [C crop](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p142_C.png)
is under a November 6 heading:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
C) NKJ v LP (09.00 p.m., November 6th)
FUER UKS 1915 (6/11)
RICHI-242
```

</details>

The 242-slot source contains two printed dashes. The unchanged published
`Nov4-6` key fixes 119 of 121 raw positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
?NXNXOXMACKENSENXENTENTEMELDETX5011XERNEUTRUMAENISCHE?ESETZUNGDERXDOBRU2SCHAXSTELLUNGSNAHMEERBETENXABTXFREMDEHEERED17U560
```

</details>

One known-coordinate substitution and two dash fills give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ANXNXOXMACKENSENXENTENTEMELDETX5011XERNEUTRUMAENISCHEBESETZUNGDERXDOBRUDSCHAXSTELLUNGSNAHMEERBETENXABTXFREMDEHEERED17U560
```

</details>

Readable core, with the reference retained literally:

**Readable German:**

> An N.O. Mackensen. Entente meldet `5011` erneut rumänische Besetzung
> der Dobrudscha. Stellungsnahme [Stellungnahme] erbeten. Abt. Fremde Heere `D17U560`.

The numerical/reference labels **`5011`** and **`D17U560`** remain as read.
They are not normalized into dates or message numbers. The raw `2` within
`DOBRU2SCHA` is retained in the raw reading and explicitly repaired locally
to `D`; this does not reassign the square's digit `2`.

Both machine layers retain `STELLUNGSNAHME`. The bracketed
**[Stellungnahme]** is a prose-only spelling normalization: its omitted `S`
is not an additional source-coordinate repair or a change to the edited
output above.

| Source index, zero-based | Printed group / position, one-based | Change | Treatment |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 2 / 4 | `G` → `F` | Known-coordinate substitution: `2` → `D` in the place name |
| 34 | 7 / 5 | printed dash → `V` | Source-erasure fill: `B` in `BESETZUNG` |
| 84 | 17 / 5 | printed dash → `V` | Source-erasure fill: initial `A` in `AN` |

The source length, transposition and full published square are unchanged.
The [certificate](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/certificates.json)
includes every source-coordinate origin and the exact reconstructed witness.

```sh
python experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/verify.py --verify
```

The key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno
Wacker**, [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
with provenance in the [inputs](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/inputs.json).
Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates existed. The bounded paper review
does not establish universal first-decipherment priority; exact arithmetic
does not prove unique historical wording or independent truth of the report.
